newsitem.title: USA: CSCE amends futures and options closing procedures.
newsitem.headline: CSCE amends futures and options closing procedures.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said on Tuesday that it ammended trading hours for futures and options commodities contracts, effective July 1.
The exchange said the revisions will reduce the closing period for futures from a five-minute to a two-minute period.

Trading hours on all options will be changed to eliminate the rotational closing call and establish a closing period of two minutes conducted simultaineously with the option's correlating futures contract, it said.
"The closing call for options contracts will be replaced with a two-minute closing period in which trading in all contract months will cease at the same time," CSCE said in a statement.

"Consequently, options trading will no longer be suspended prior to the close," it said. "Instead, trading will flow directly into the closing period. With these amendments, options contracts will now trade during the same hous as their corresponding futures contracts."
Exchange spokesman Terence Gordon said the changes should facilitate trading for CSCE customers by simplifying options and futures closing procedures.
"It consolidates the trading hours for all the contracts and provides members and the trade with a little uniformity," said Gorden.
